items.requirement: State the research question as finding the minimum worst-case multiclass 0–1 loss achievable by a soft classifier for a fixed finite-support distribution and a specified test-time perturbation model.
items.quote:
we characterize the optimal 0 − 1 loss for any discrete distribution (e.g. training set)
in the presence of a test-time attacker.

items.requirement: Identify the empirical training samples used in the main experiments. The three-class runs use MNIST digits 1, 4, and 7 and CIFAR-10 plane, bird, and ship, with 1,000 samples per class. The ten-class bounds use the full training sets.
items.quote:
for 3-class MNIST (classes ‘1’, ‘4’, ‘7’) and 3-class CIFAR-10 (‘plane’, ‘bird’ and ‘ship’ classes)

items.requirement: Report robust 0–1 loss across test-time ℓ₂ perturbation budgets ϵ and identify the three-class baseline as TRADES adversarial training evaluated with APGD-CE from AutoAttack.
items.quote: We evaluate models using APGD-CE from AutoAttack (9).

items.requirement: Report the main empirical finding that adversarially trained classifiers showed a large robust-loss gap relative to the exact three-class optimum and the ten-class bounds, including at small tested perturbation budgets.
items.quote:
For both datasets, we see a large gap
between the performance of adversarial training and our bounds

items.requirement: Identify both ten-class lower-bound methods and their observed tradeoff. Truncated conflict hypergraphs retain hyperedges up to degree 2, 3, or 4, while maximum-weight coupling of pairwise binary optima gives a looser lower bound.
items.quote: obtained bound is much looser compared to that from truncated hypergraphs.

items.requirement: Identify the generalized Caro–Wei independent-set bound as an upper bound on optimal hard- and soft-classifier loss. Describe its close agreement with the truncated lower bounds at small tested budgets as an empirical finding.
items.quote:
the lower bounds obtained through truncated hypergraphs (L∗(2), L∗(3), and

items.requirement: State that computation becomes expensive as the perturbation budget, sample size, and number of classes grow. Frame the main empirical gap as a measure of robust fit to the training data and leave closing the gap while maintaining generalization as an open problem.
items.quote:
One major limitation of our work is the computational expense at
larger budgets, sample sizes and class sizes.
